Based on my search, I can provide you with information about the **Navy P-3**, which refers to the **Lockheed P-3 Orion**, a legendary maritime patrol aircraft used by the U.S. Navy and many other countries.

## Overview of the P-3 Orion

The **P-3 Orion** is a four-engine turboprop maritime patrol aircraft developed by Lockheed. It has been one of the most enduring and versatile military aircraft in aviation history, serving for over 50 years in various roles.

### Key Features and Capabilities

- **Primary Role**: Anti-submarine warfare (ASW), maritime patrol, and reconnaissance
- **Endurance**: Capable of flying **16-hour missions** with dash speeds up to **466 mph**
- **Detection Systems**: Equipped with magnetic anomaly detectors (MAD), sonobuoys, infrared and long-range electro-optical cameras, and special imaging radar
- **Weapons**: Large internal weapons bay and **10 external hardpoints** for torpedoes, depth charges, missiles (including Harpoon and AIM-9 Sidewinder), and mines
- **Crew**: Typically 12-person flight crew

### Historical Significance

The P-3 Orion played a crucial role during the **Cold War** as the U.S. Navy's primary anti-submarine warfare platform. Soviet Marshal Sergey Akhromeyev reportedly said: *"I always know where my submarines are. I look at where the P-3s are flying—that's where my submarines are."*

The P-3 saw extensive service in:
- **Cuban Missile Crisis** (1962) – among the first aircraft deployed
- **Vietnam War** – Operation Market Time for coastal interdiction
- **Gulf War** (1990) – monitoring Iraqi troop positions and targeting
- **Balkan wars** – electronic warfare and surveillance
- **Operation Enduring Freedom** and other post-Cold War conflicts

### Retirement and Current Status

- The **U.S. Navy retired the P-3 from active-duty patrol squadrons in 2019**, replacing it with the **Boeing P-8A Poseidon**
- As of **October 2025**, only **six active U.S. Navy P-3s remain** in specialized units:
  - **VX-30**: 4 aircraft (150521, 160293, 162999, 163291)
  - **VXS-1**: 2 aircraft (158570, 158912)
- **NOAA** continues to operate two WP-3D "hurricane hunter" aircraft nicknamed *Kermit* and *Miss Piggy* for atmospheric research

### International Operators

The P-3 remains in service with numerous international operators, including:
- **Canada** (CP-140 Aurora/CP-140M)
- **Portugal** – modernizing P-3C CUP II aircraft with €24 million investment (2025-2028)
- **Argentina** – receiving additional P-3C aircraft (second delivered October 2025, more expected in 2026)
- **South Korea** – upgrading P-3C fleet with improved satellite communications
- **Japan, Germany (formerly), Netherlands, and others**

### Civilian and Scientific Uses

Beyond military applications, P-3s have been adapted for:
- **Hurricane hunting** (NOAA)
- **Aerial firefighting** (though P-3A Aerostar firefighting aircraft are being phased out)
- **Oil spill monitoring** (BP Horizon disaster response)
- **Various research missions**

The P-3 Orion represents one of the most successful and adaptable military aircraft designs ever produced, with over **750 units built** by Lockheed and Kawasaki combined.

---

Sources:
1. https://airandspace.si.edu/air-and-space-quarterly/issue-13/orion-p3
2. https://www.lockheedmartin.com/en-us/products/p-3.html
3. https://www.p3orion.nl/news.html
4. https://www.stratasys.com/it/industries-and-applications/3d-printing-industries/government/
5. https://www.washington.edu/news/2005/08/08/rainbands-and-hurricane-intensity-collaborative-hurricane-research-project-ultimately-could-improve-forecasting/
